translationRepairs: His father Gunazan served the Taizong. On the campaign against the Ming, below Datong he stormed Little Stone City and was first over the wall. He was granted the title "Baturu" and a hereditary rank as niru janggin.

His father Gunazan served the Taizong. On the campaign against the Ming, when the army halted at Datong, he stormed Little Stone City and was first over the wall. He was granted the title "Baturu" and a hereditary rank as niru janggin.
In military narrative 次大同 means the army halted or encamped at Datong, not that the assault took place 'below' the city; the proposed rendering matches 次 followed by 攻小石城.
Governor Fu Honglie was defeated by Wu Sangui's general Wu Shijiong, and Manggitu marched to join forces with him.
Governor Fu Honglie was defeated by Wu Sangui's general Wu Shicong, and Manggitu marched to join forces with him.
The given name is 琮, read cóng, so Wu Shicong is required; Shijiong would need a different graph such as 炯.
The army advanced and took Nanning. The rebel Ma Chengzhao united with Wu Sangui's troops to some one hundred thousand men and offered battle.
The army advanced and took Nanning. The rebel Ma Chengyin united with Wu Sangui's troops to some one hundred thousand men and offered battle.
馬承廕 uses 廕 (yìn); Chengzhao has no support in the characters, and Chengyin restores the name.
In year 19 Manggitu died in camp. Gu Badai followed Pacification of the South Grand General Ceben south into Yunnan to besiege the provincial capital.
In year 19 Manggitu died in camp. Gu Badai followed Pacification of the South Grand General Laita south into Yunnan to besiege the provincial capital.
賚塔 is Laita; Ceben does not correspond to these characters.

Gansu Provincial Commander Zhang Yong asked to slow the advance; the emperor ordered Tulai to hold the passes at Fengxiang, Qinzhou, and other key points, detach troops to Pacification of the South General Muzhan's descent on Huguang, and ordered Ma Erhan to follow.

Gansu Provincial Commander Zhang Yong asked to slow the advance; the emperor ordered Tulai to hold the passes at Fengxiang, Qinzhou, and other key points, detach troops to General Who Campaigns South Muzhan's descent on Huguang, and ordered Ma Erhan to follow.
征南將軍 is not 平南, so 'Pacification of the South' is wrong, but 'Conquest-the-South General' is an awkward calque; the established rendering is General Who Campaigns South.
In year 26 he was appointed Director of the Court of Colonial Affairs.
In year 26 he was appointed Secretary of the Court of Colonial Affairs.
理籓院司務 is the secretaryship (司務) of the Court of Colonial Affairs, not a director-level post.
In the twenty-sixth year he was appointed Director of the Court of Colonial Affairs.
In the twenty-sixth year he was appointed Secretary of the Court of Colonial Affairs.
The literal line has the same rank error: 司務 is a secretary, not Director of the Court of Colonial Affairs.
He was promoted again to Minister of War, made a lecturer at the Classics Colloquium, and named a Grand Councilor.
He was promoted again to Minister of War, made a lecturer at the Classics Colloquium, and named a Deliberative Minister.
議政大臣 belongs to the Deliberative Council; Grand Councilor would be 軍機大臣, an office not named here.
He was again promoted to Minister of War, appointed lecturer at the Classics Colloquium, and enrolled among the Grand Councilors.
He was again promoted to Minister of War, appointed lecturer at the Classics Colloquium, and enrolled among the Deliberative Ministers.
The literal likewise equates 議政大臣 with Grand Councilors; Deliberative Ministers is the correct office.

In Kangxi year 35 the emperor campaigned in person against Galdan and stationed Ma Erhan at Tumubao to manage relay posts. Because the army horses supplied were in poor condition, the personnel office recommended dismissal, but the emperor showed leniency.

In Kangxi year 35 the emperor campaigned in person against Galdan and stationed Ma Erhan at Tumu to manage relay posts. Because the army horses supplied were in poor condition, the personnel office recommended dismissal, but the emperor showed leniency.
The place is written 土木; Tumubao adds an unstated 堡.

In the thirty-fifth year the emperor campaigned in person against Galdan and ordered Ma Erhan to remain at Tumubao to oversee relay stations; because the army horses sent were weak, the personnel office recommended stripping his office, but the emperor ordered leniency.

In the thirty-fifth year the emperor campaigned in person against Galdan and ordered Ma Erhan to remain at Tumu to oversee relay stations; because the army horses sent were weak, the personnel office recommended stripping his office, but the emperor ordered leniency.
The literal also inflates 土木 into Tumubao; Tumu follows the Chinese.
He memorialized, "At home I read the imperial edict clearing Suksaha, whom Oboi destroyed out of enmity, killing his sons and grandsons and implicating Bai'erhetu's clan by association.
He memorialized, "At home I read the imperial edict clearing Suksaha, whom Oboi destroyed out of enmity, killing his sons and grandsons and implicating the clansman Bai'erhetu by association.
連坐族人白爾赫圖 names Bai'erhetu as the implicated clansman; 'Bai'erhetu's clan' inverts 族人.

He memorialized: "At home I read the imperial edict clearing Suksaha, who was framed and destroyed by Oboi out of enmity, killing his sons and grandsons and implicating the clan of Bai'erhetu by association.

He memorialized: "At home I read the imperial edict clearing Suksaha, who was framed and destroyed by Oboi out of enmity, killing his sons and grandsons and implicating the clansman Bai'erhetu by association.
The literal's 'clan of Bai'erhetu' misreads 族人白爾赫圖, which is the kinsman himself.
He was transferred to Intendant of Shuntian Prefecture.
He was transferred to Prefect of Shuntian Prefecture.
順天府尹 is the metropolitan prefect (yin), not an intendant.
He was transferred to Intendant of Shuntian Prefecture.
He was transferred to Prefect of Shuntian Prefecture.
The literal repeats the same office error for 府尹.
Jin Shengzong rebelled in Jiangxi and Jiang Xian in Datong—no different from Geng Jingzhong and Wang Fuchen.
Jin Shenghuan rebelled in Jiangxi and Jiang Xiang in Datong—no different from Geng Jingzhong and Wang Fuchen.
金聲桓 is Jin Shenghuan and 姜瓖 is Jiang Xiang; Shengzong and Xian do not match the graphs.
Jin Shengzong rebelled in Jiangxi and Jiang Xian in Datong—no different from Geng Jingzhong and Wang Fuchen.
Jin Shenghuan rebelled in Jiangxi and Jiang Xiang in Datong—no different from Geng Jingzhong and Wang Fuchen.
The literal carries the same mistranscriptions of 聲桓 and 瓖.
Circuit intendants pay annual gifts to prefects, who add exactions on top, so the officials and people under a prefect are virtually sold to him.
Circuits and prefectures pay annual customary gifts, and with additional squeezing the officials and people under them are virtually sold to those circuits and prefectures.
道府歲納規禮 makes circuits and prefectures the payers of customary gifts; the original invents circuit intendants paying prefects, and 道府所轄官民 are sold to those 道府.
Circuit intendants pay annual customary gifts to prefects, who add exactions on top, so the officials and people under a prefect are no better than sold to the prefect.
Circuits and prefectures pay annual customary gifts, and with additional squeezing the officials and people under the circuits and prefectures are no better than sold to them.
The literal likewise turns 道府 into a circuit-to-prefect payment that the Chinese does not state.
Prefectures and counties pay annual gifts to circuit intendants, who add extortion on top, so the gentry and people under a county are virtually sold to it.
Departments and counties pay annual customary gifts, and with further extortion the gentry and people under them are virtually sold to those departments and counties.
州縣歲納規禮 does not say prefectures pay circuit intendants; 州縣所屬士民 are sold to the departments and counties themselves.
Prefectures and counties pay annual gifts to circuit intendants, who add extortion on top, so the gentry and people under a county are no better than sold to the county.
Departments and counties pay annual customary gifts, and with further extortion the gentry and people belonging to them are no better than sold to the departments and counties.
The added 'to circuit intendants' is absent from 州縣歲納規禮; the literal should keep departments and counties as both payers and beneficiaries of the squeeze.

In the Shunzhi reign, Shandong surveillance commissioner Cheng Heng impeached Governor Geng Tun, and Jiangnan surveillance commissioner Qin Shizhen impeached Tu Guobao—both received heavy punishment, and the empire was awed.

In the Shunzhi reign, Shandong regional inspector Cheng Heng impeached Governor Geng Tun, and Jiangnan regional inspector Qin Shizhen impeached Tu Guobao—both received heavy punishment, and the empire was awed.
巡按 is the regional inspector; surveillance commissioner would be 按察使.

In the Shizu reign, Shandong Surveillance Commissioner Cheng Heng impeached Governor Geng Tun, and Jiangnan Surveillance Commissioner Qin Shizhen impeached Tu Guobao—both received heavy punishment, and all under Heaven were awed.

In the Shizu reign, Shandong Regional Inspector Cheng Heng impeached Governor Geng Tun, and Jiangnan Regional Inspector Qin Shizhen impeached Tu Guobao—both received heavy punishment, and all under Heaven were awed.
The literal should render both 巡按 posts as Regional Inspector, matching 山東巡按 and 江南巡按.

When Kinmen and Xiamen were pacified, Governor Yao Qisheng asked that land beyond the boundary be returned by household register, maritime prohibitions relaxed, and profits from fish and salt used for military supplies; court ministers opposed it.

When Kinmen and Xiamen were pacified, Governor-General Yao Qisheng asked that land beyond the boundary be returned by household register, maritime prohibitions relaxed, and profits from fish and salt used for military supplies; court ministers opposed it.
總督姚啟聖 is a governor-general, a higher office than governor (巡撫).

After they arrived, Wu Sangui plotted rebellion. Provincial Commander Li Benshen joined the plot and wrote to recruit Guizhou Governor Cao Shenji. Governor-General Gan Wenxuan learned of it, informed Sa Muha and the others, urged them to hurry to the capital to report the rebellion, and asked for relief troops.

After they arrived, Wu Sangui plotted rebellion. Provincial Commander Li Benshen joined the plot and wrote to recruit Guizhou Governor Cao Shenji. Governor-General Gan Wenkun learned of it, informed Sa Muha and the others, urged them to hurry to the capital to report the rebellion, and asked for relief troops.
焜 is kūn, so the personal name is Gan Wenkun, not Gan Wenxuan.

In year 14, in accounting merit for reporting the rebellion, Sa Muha, Dangwuli, and Xilantai were all due for promotion to minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud, and similar posts.

In year 14, in accounting merit for reporting the rebellion, Sa Muha, Dangwuli, and Xilantai were all due for promotion to minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud, and similar posts.
光祿 here is the Court of Imperial Entertainments (光祿寺); the Court of Imperial Sacrifices is 太常寺.
Before long Bin entered service as Minister and memorialized, "The sea mouth need not be dredged urgently; if flood comes again, downstream prefectures and counties will all be submerged."
Before long Bin entered service as Minister and memorialized, "If the sea mouth is not dredged promptly, should flood come again, the downstream prefectures and counties will all be submerged."
海口不急濬 is the negative condition whose consequence is 再遇水…悉付巨浸, not advice that dredging need not be urgent; Tang Bin is warning against delay.

Before long Bin entered service as Minister and memorialized: "The sea mouth need not be dredged urgently; if water comes again, the downstream prefectures and counties will all be given to vast flooding."

Before long Bin entered service as Minister and memorialized: "If the sea mouth is not urgently dredged, should water come again, the downstream prefectures and counties will all be given over to vast flooding."
The literal inverts 不急濬 into 'need not be dredged urgently,' reversing the warning that follows from leaving the sea mouth undredged.
